Now let me give a brief overview of the company's performance for the second quarter and the 
half year ended September 30, 2026. The group has achieved a turnover of INR1,215.99 crores 
for the second quarter as compared to INR1,128.21 crores for the corresponding quarter of the 
previous year, achieving a value growth of 7.8% on the back of a double-digit volume growth.  
The value growth because of the green coffee prices coming down, the value growth trails the 
volume growth, which stands at double-digit. The EBITDA stands at INR217.3 crores as against 
INR198.6 crores, which is a growth of 9.5%, while the profit before tax is INR150.86 crores, 
growing at 18.7% and the net profit stands at INR130 crores with a growth of almost 29%. 
As far as H1 is concerned, the group has achieved a turnover of INR2,419.58 crores as compared 
to INR2,186.25 crores, which is a growth of approximately 11.6%. The EBITDA stands at 
INR414 crores as against INR360 crores, which is a growth of almost 15%. And the PBT, which 
is at INR279.88 crores is growing at 26.48% and the net profit, which is at INR246.96 crores for 
the first half is growing at 42%. 
The domestic business has achieved a gross turnover of INR210 crores this quarter, out of which 
the brand sales is approximately INR140 crores. The good part is that the growth momentum for 
the branded business continues, and we are growing at 25%, and we look forward to maintain 
this kind of a growth momentum going forward as well. 
As far as the green coffee prices are concerned, while it is still fluctuating, but has been range 
bound in the region of USD3,400 to USD3,800 per ton. And the Vietnam crop, which is slated
